purpose: Pexidartinib is used to treat adults with a rare tumor called tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT). This is a non-cancerous but often painful tumor that grows in or around joints, most commonly the knee. It is used when the tumor is causing severe symptoms and cannot be fully removed by surgery.
how_it_works: This medicine works by blocking a specific protein signal in the body called CSF1R, which tells certain abnormal cells to grow and multiply out of control. By blocking this signal, the drug slows or stops the growth of the tumor cells. Think of it like turning off a switch that the tumor cells need to keep growing.
common_side_effects: Hair color changes (lighter hair), fatigue or tiredness, nausea, swelling in the face or hands, changes in taste, decreased appetite, muscle or joint pain, constipation, skin rash, and abnormal results on liver blood tests.
warnings: This medication carries a serious risk of liver damage, which can be life-threatening. Because of this risk, it is only available through a special program called a REMS program, and you will need regular blood tests to check your liver while taking it. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, or stomach pain. Avoid alcohol and other medications that can harm the liver. Do not use if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby — use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after stopping.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg capsules) taken by mouth twice a day, with food. Try to take it at the same times each day. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or open them. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects or liver problems.
